description: Core-owned, technology-independent golden vectors proving that today's Python (modules/calculations.py) and JavaScript (web/js/calc.js) implementations of six shared calculations produce the same result on the same valid input. Tests raw calculation semantics, not UI/display formatting -- except for inverse Tinseth, whose production functions round to 1 decimal internally (see tolerance_principle below).
tolerance_principle: Absolute tolerance per calculation type, chosen as the smallest value robust across Python (CPython math/pow) and JavaScript (V8 Math.exp/Math.pow) double-precision floating point -- not a large tolerance chosen to hide a real deviation. og/fg_abv use only +,-,*,/ (no transcendental functions), so both runtimes are expected to agree to full double precision: tolerance 1e-9. ebc_morey and tinseth_ibu involve a fractional-exponent power (Math.pow/** 0.6859) and/or exp (Math.exp/math.exp), which can differ by a few ULPs between runtimes' underlying libm/JS-engine implementations: tolerance 1e-6 absolute, still ~7-8 significant digits of agreement at these calculations' typical magnitude (10-70). inverse_tinseth's production functions (beregn_gram_fra_ibu / beregnGramFraIBU) round their own output to 1 decimal as part of the existing, unchanged calculation contract (not a UI-layer concern) -- as of the PRI 1 QA correction (CALC-002), BOTH implementations round with decimal half-up, so golden vectors now require near-exact agreement against that already-rounded contractual output: tolerance 1e-9, deliberately NOT 0.05 (half the 0.1 rounding grain), since a tolerance that wide could let two adjacent, equally-plausible-looking 1-decimal contractual results both pass the same vector -- see inverse_tinseth_tie_case_half_up, which is deliberately constructed to land exactly on a .x5 tie boundary and would have caught the old Python round-half-to-even vs JS Math.round-half-up divergence this correction fixed. measured_abv (issue #77, standalone ABV calculator) uses only +,-,*,/ for both the standard and high-gravity estimates -- no transcendental functions -- so both runtimes are expected to agree to full double precision, same as og/fg_abv: tolerance 1e-9.

canonical_units.potential_sg: malt potential as specific gravity, e.g. 1.037
canonical_units.ebc: malt or beer color in degrees EBC
canonical_units.efficiency_fraction: mash efficiency as a 0-1 fraction, e.g. 0.75 for 75%
canonical_units.attenuation_fraction: yeast apparent attenuation as a 0-1 fraction
canonical_units.alpha_acid_percent: hop alpha acid as a percent number, e.g. 12.0 for 12%
canonical_units.wort_gravity_sg: wort gravity (typically OG) as specific gravity
canonical_units.target_ibu: desired IBU contribution from one hop addition
canonical_units.abv_percent: alcohol by volume as a percent number
canonical_units.hop_amount_g: grams of hops, rounded to 1 decimal by the production functions themselves
canonical_units.abv_standard_percent: standard ABV estimate ((OG-FG)*131.25) from measured OG+FG, as a percent number
canonical_units.abv_high_gravity_percent: alternate high-gravity ABV estimate from measured OG+FG, as a percent number

cases.note: Compares against the production function's own rounded (1 decimal) output -- see tolerance_principle. cases.description: CALC-002 (PRI 1 QA correction): target_ibu is deliberately chosen so the RAW pre-rounding gram value is exactly 10.25 (raw*10 = 102.5, an exact 1-decimal rounding tie in IEEE754 double precision -- verified programmatically, not approximate). Old Python round(10.25, 1) [bankers'/half-even rounding] gave 10.2; JavaScript's existing Math.round(102.5)/10 [half-up] gives 10.3. This vector proves the corrected Python implementation (decimal half-up, matching JavaScript) now also gives 10.3 -- it would have failed against the pre-CALC-002 Python code.
cases.note: Deliberately ON a .x5 rounding tie boundary (raw value 10.25 exactly) -- the opposite of every other inverse_tinseth case, which are deliberately verified to sit AWAY from one. This is the case that actually exercises the half-up vs half-even distinction.

cases.description: Normal-strength beer, measured OG/FG directly (no recipe) -- acceptance criterion 5, issue #77. Standard estimate matches the issue's own worked example (~4.59% before display rounding).

High-gravity/imperial-strength case, deliberately chosen around OG 1.100 / FG 1.022 (a representative Vardeldr-like strong beer, issue #77 acceptance criterion 6) -- demonstrates the material (~1.08 percentage point) difference between the standard and high-gravity estimates that motivates surfacing both explicitly instead of silently switching formulas.

Second, independent high-gravity example (OG 1.090 / FG 1.015) isolating a different OG/FG pair from measured_abv_high_gravity_vaardeldr -- both estimates still meaningfully diverge (~0.8 percentage points).

OG 1.070 -- the UI presentation threshold this issue's implementation chose for surfacing the high-gravity estimate alongside the standard one (see web/verktoy.html / ui/abv_calculator_panel.py). Both Core estimates are always computed regardless of this UI trigger; this vector only proves they remain correct exactly at the boundary value.
